page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text; a decorative woodcut rule between the text and the division heading; a marginal note at the left margin beside the first line of the chapter opening ("Rom.1.c").

main_text.p: nam confirmare, est cam incertiorem, quàm dudum, reddere.

Tertium, quòd ex voce אלהים (quæ plurali numero ab Hebraeis prolata, tamen cum verbo singulari ברא coniungitur. Genes.1.versiculo 1.) Quod item ex trina benedictione, quæ in Psal.67.verf.1.&6.&7. diuersis locis repetitur, colligit Lombardus ad eiusdem articuli tam vexati fidem faciendam, est ieiunum & exile, ne dicam ἀσυλλόγιστον, quum Hebraei, ex linguæ suæ vsu, in honorabilioribus personis designandis, alibi quoque pluralem numerum pro singulari vsurpare soleant, non quidem alicuius diuini mysterij significandi gratiâ, sed dignitatis tantum illorum amplificandæ causâ: & trina illa benedictio sit duntaxat vehementis precationis indicium, & vbertas in eo Psalmo: non vllius mysterij arcana significatio, ac sacramentum. Confer cum cap.1.&2. nostræ synopseos infrà.

main_text.p: Rom.1.cA Postolus nanque ait, quòd inuisibilia Dei a creatura mundi, per ea quæ facta sunt, intellecta conspiciuntur, sempiterna quoque virtus eius, & diui-

page.notes: The Hebrew word in the first paragraph is printed as אלהים with a following word ברא; the Greek word in the middle of the second paragraph is a partial reading. The opening letter "A" of the chapter is a large decorative initial. Pages below the text are blank. Marginal note "Rom.1.c" is transcribed as printed; its mark is a small sign.
